name: avon
title: Avon, New York
frame: x=east z=south y=up, metres, origin at centre

signs.text: PIZZA LAND — EST. 1960 — THE BEST PIZZA ANYWHERE
PIZZA LAND — EST. 1960 — THE BEST PIZZA ANYWHERE

blueprint._comment: 40 East Main St (corner of North Avenue): big grey-sided 2.5-storey American Foursquare. Pyramidal hip roof with hipped dormers on the front, east and west slopes, centre chimney; full-width front porch on Tuscan columns (+u, East Main), which continues along the east side as a porte-cochere over the driveway (-v). Two-storey square bay on the North Avenue face (+v). Two-storey gabled rear wing and a one-storey hip kitchen wing at the north-west corner, small rear stoop at the north-east. Black shutters, white trim. Road face by distance is +v (North Avenue); the real front is +u.

121 Genesee St: white clapboard 2.5-storey American Foursquare. Hip roof in dark grey-green shingle, a wide green-shingled front gable dormer (roof.dormers on the hip's -v slope) with a round-arched window, red brick chimney right of the dormer, full-width open porch with white posts and railing and centred steps to a dark front door. Rear wing carries a cross gable whose end (with a small arched attic window) faces the +u driveway side. Road face -v; left (0) = +u = SSW (away from 119 Genesee).

119 Genesee St: 2.5-storey olive Queen Anne with a hip roof, a steep front gable (arched attic window) over the left half of the street face, cross gables on both long sides, a full-width open porch with white posts and railing, red steps, and a round-arched siding opening at the right end of the porch leading to the dark red front door. Stone foundation. Road face +u; left (0) = +v = SSW (toward 121 Genesee).

102 Genesee St (The Foot Doctor): greige gable-front 2-storey block on the SSW half, 1.5-storey cross-gabled wing on the NNE half, full-width white open porch (top-level, spanning both front volumes on the shared wall u=6.2) with a small gabled entry pediment, 1-storey rear wing behind the wing. +u = street (WNW), +v = NNE.

porches._comment: full-width front porch across both front volumes; left (NNE, +v) to right fractions along the porch; steps centred on the door at v=0.76

blueprint._comment: T's On Genesee Market & Deli, 90 Genesee St. White clapboard 2-storey flat-roofed commercial block, sage-green window trim, bracketed cornice, storefront on a tan-brick kick with red (umbrella) accents. Road face +u. Volume is 1 m narrower than the OBB on the +v side to leave the real ~2.3 m alley to the laundromat (78).

Coyne Econ-O-Wash laundromat, 78 Genesee St. Tall white-clapboard Second Empire front on a red-brick storefront base: bracketed cornice, black mansard (front section only), pedimented gable with oculus on top, two hooded upper windows, gold-on-black sign. A white gabled block with a brick-based rear runs behind. Road face -u. Volumes stop 1 m short of the OBB on the +v side to leave the real ~2.3 m alley to T's (90).

volumes._comment: Thin post hidden inside the mansard; it only exists to carry the pediment up onto the mansard cap.

blueprint._comment: Community Bank, 68 Genesee St. Low tan-sided branch on a red-brick base, shallow dark gable, glass atrium at the NW corner, tan clock tower at the north end of the street face, clerestory monitor along the ridge, drive-through canopy on the north side.

storeys._comment: Central pane and continuous pale circular tracery plate. Keep the eight surrounding panes.

blueprint._comment: 60 South Ave: small one-storey slate-teal vinyl ranch under a low side-gable roof (ridge along the frontage), chimney just left of centre on the ridge. Front (road face +v, left = -u = NNE): wide picture window left, dark front door with a sidelight under a white metal shed awning right of centre, twin window at the right end, black iron step rails. Open flat-roofed carport attached to the rear half of the -u (NNE) gable end = the polygon's back-left wing. Gable ends have a small attic vent and one window. The yellow two-storey house in the -u_3 / -v photos is the neighbour to the north, not this building.

38 South Ave: raised ranch / split-entry. Lower storey red-brown brick, upper storey pale yellow vinyl siding, low dark-brown gable roof with the ridge along the street (gable ends on +u/-u). Road face +v: upper storey has a wide triple window left, a small window centre, a window right over the garage; lower storey has a window left, the white front door just right of centre at grade, and a dark brown single garage door at the right end. Lot rises ~1.2 m toward the rear so the brick lower storey is half-buried behind. Left (0) of +v = -u = NNE.

South Ave (west side, north of 60 South): white clapboard two-storey Greek Revival farmhouse with black shutters and a tall green-painted foundation. Side-gabled main block (ridge along u, gable ends on +u/-u) with a front-facing cross gable with cornice returns over the NNE (+u) end of the road face and a grey exterior chimney at that corner. Set-back one-storey hip-roofed wing at the +u (NNE) end with a red-railed open deck in the notch between wing and block; 4 shuttered upper windows in a row on the road face, wide window right. Road face -v; left (0) = +u = NNE. The white 2-storey house with a white lattice deck in the foreground of +u_3 is the northern neighbour, not this building.

20 South Ave: narrow 2-storey gable-front house in pale grey-white vinyl with white trim, gable end to the road, two 1/1 windows per storey stacked in two bays, no door on the road face. Entry is a raised white-railed deck on the -v (NNE, driveway) side near the road end, reached by a white stair that faces the road (number 20 on the newel). Dark grey shingle roof, boxed eaves with returns, no chimney. Road face -u; left (0) = -v = NNE (driveway / garage 248252373 side). The open garage in the -v photos is the neighbour 248252373.

Detached two-bay garage beside 20 South Ave (OSM tags it 'house', but every photo shows a single-storey open-front garage here, 3.3 m NNE of house 248252370 across its driveway). Gable end to the road, ridge along u, black asphalt shingles; walls are bare OSB sheathing under torn white housewrap, concrete block base; two open bays with a centre pier, no doors. Road face -u; left (0) = -v = NNE. The cream house in the -v photos is the next house north, not this building.

Corner house at West Main St / South Ave (no address in OSM; the house NW of 51 West Main). Long greige vinyl two-storey house under a dark grey gable roof with the ridge running along u (perpendicular to West Main). Real front = +u (NE, toward West Main): full-width open porch with white posts and railing, a white front door with steps at right-centre, and a dark green second door at the left end (in reality reached by a stair with a little gable hood); upstairs two windows, the left one with rust shutters. The porch wraps a short way onto the -v (South Ave) side. Rear (-u, SW) gable end carries an enclosed screened sun porch on the upper floor, a row of screen panels under the gable, standing over an open undercroft on posts. Road face per pipeline is -v (South Ave); left (0) of -v = NE end.

51 West Main Street: greige clapboard two-storey house, gable end to West Main (+u, the real front; ridge along u), dark grey roof. Signature: a tall round-arched window with a white fan head and dark green shutters in the front gable, a second green-shuttered window beside it, a full-width open porch with white posts and railing, and an exterior stair up the +v (SE) side to a second-floor door under a small cross gable with a little balcony and flag. Road face per pipeline is -v (South Ave) but that side is hidden behind 248252380; left (0) of -v = NE end.

House on the south side of West Main St between 51 W Main and Rivoli Dental: a white clapboard L-plan Victorian. Road face -v (NE); left (0) = +u = SE toward Rivoli Dental. Left ~55% is a two-storey side-gabled block with a one-storey open porch on turned posts with gingerbread brackets (front door at the porch's right end against the wing, wreathed window at left, two tall windows above). Right ~45% is a steep front-gabled wing stepping ~1.5 m forward: a wide three-part window below, two hooded windows above and a lacy gingerbread bargeboard with a sunburst at the apex. Dark grey shingle roofs. Lower rear section behind with a side door under a small canopy on the NW side.

29 West Main St: 2-storey pale-yellow clapboard house, front gable toward the street (-u, NE), grey-blue shutters, dark brown shingle roof. Enclosed one-storey sun porch across the left (SE, -v) half of the front with a wide window band; front door with '29' beside it and one shuttered window to the right; two shuttered windows upstairs. Long lower rear wing / attached garage running SW to the parking area. Honey-locust in the front yard.

90 West Main St (White Horse Automotive): tan stucco one-storey flat-roofed auto-repair shop on the corner of Rochester St (-v) and West Main (-u). L-shaped: a long strip along Rochester St with a ROUNDED glassy corner at the Rochester/West Main end (stair-stepped boxes here), plus a rear wing along West Main. Darker tan belt band at window-head height, dark-brown coping. Roll-up bays face the parking lot (+v, unseen). Yellow 'Registered Motor Vehicle Repair Shop' signs and a round black horse logo on the West Main side.

35 Rochester St (behind 90 W Main): white-grey corrugated-metal pole barn / fleet garage, gable end to Rochester St (-v). Signature: a deep open steel portal-frame canopy (rust-brown posts and rafters) carrying the roof out over the apron, sheltering two big roll-up bays plus a narrower third bay at the right. Light sage-green band along the eaves, light-grey low-pitch metal gable roof, ridge street-to-rear. Plain grey man-door on the NNE side (+u) behind a white vinyl fence. The tan stucco office building on the right (SSW) is the neighbour 248273879 (90 West Main), not this building.

Saint Agnes School office (old parish house), Prospect St: two-storey white clapboard Greek Revival under a low hip roof with a deep entablature band and two small stacks, a monumental two-storey portico with four round columns recessed across the whole road face (columns at the front plane, wall set back), stone foundation with lattice, wide grey stair up to the centred front door with transom, light blue-grey shutters on the front ground windows. One-storey rear section with a hip roof, then a narrower one-storey gabled wing on the NNE (+u) half. Red 'SAINT AGNES SCHOOL' lawn sign right of the front walk. Road face -v; left (0) = +u = NNE.

91 Prospect St: white clapboard 2-storey gable-front-and-wing farmhouse with slate-blue shutters, a dark grey roof, a brick chimney where the front cross-gable meets the main ridge, and a big white wraparound porch (teal lattice skirt, turned posts) across the street face and back along the SSW side. The street face has a full-height front gable over its left (SSW) half with two tiny attic lights; a one-storey hip-roofed north wing with a street-facing garage tucked under it (the drive digs down); low rear service wing. Road face +u; left (0) = +v = SSW (toward the mint 77 Prospect).

100 Prospect Street: two-storey red-brick gable-front house set far back from the street on the St. Agnes side, gable end (ridge along u) facing Prospect. Signature: round wheel window in the peak, white-shuttered upper windows, white pedimented door hood on two columns over an off-centre (right of centre) white door with oval glass, small square ground-floor windows and a brass lamp. Road face -u; left (0) = -v = NNE (toward the school). The +u/+v photos show brown-shingled houses on the next street, not this building.

signs.text: UNITED STATES POST OFFICE  AVON, NEW YORK

blueprint._comment: 53 Prospect St: pale-yellow vinyl-clapboard two-family, dark-red shutters, tan/brown shingle roofs. Street face (+u, E): the south ~55% is a side-gabled 2-storey block (ridge N-S) fronted by a full-width one-storey porch with a low hip roof on four heavy timber posts on stacked-stone piers, two front doors (white left, dark red right) and a small shuttered window pair upstairs; the north ~45% is a 2-storey front-facing gable wing, flush with the main block, with two shuttered windows upstairs and a shutter-flanked three-light bay window below (faces[].bays). A tall red-brick exterior chimney stands on the south wall at the back of the 2-storey block; a long one-storey rear wing runs west (downhill) toward the detached garage 248274489. Road face +u; left (0) = +v = S. The cream Victorian with the gabled turned-post porch in the -v photos is the neighbour 248273915, not this house.

West side of Prospect Street between 53 and 77 Prospect: pale-yellow clapboard 1.5-storey farmhouse under a medium-grey roof whose ridge runs parallel to the street (gable ends face the neighbours; the south gable end has two storeys of windows plus an attic window), with a small steep cross gable centred on the street face and a full-width open front porch with white turned posts and a spindle railing (hammock in the right bay). Dark-green window trim. A lower rear kitchen wing fills the back of the 19.7 m deep footprint. Road face +u; left (0) = +v = SSW (toward 53 Prospect). The one-storey pale-green metal-roofed addition and the 2-storey green house right of the porch in the +u photo belong to 77 Prospect (248273917), not this building.

77 Prospect St: odd little pale-mint vinyl house. Street face (-u, left = -v = SSW toward the cream Victorian at 248273915) reads left to right: a one-storey flat-roofed wing with a white door and a wall lamp; a taller 1.5-storey block under a steep bright standing-seam metal gable (ridge parallel to the street, gable ends to +/-v) with one wide triple window and two small high windows; a tiny white-posted metal-roofed entry portico with brick planters at the right end; then an open-fronted carport (a real top-level carport porch: two white posts at the street end, silver gable to the street, asphalt slab) at the NNE end. Rear (+u) is a low flat-roofed extension, unseen; kept plain.

porches._comment: open carport beside the main block's NNE wall: backs onto u=0 (open air behind), runs 6.7 m out to the street line; gable ridge runs out from the wall so the gable end faces the street

blueprint._comment: 84 Prospect St: Frontier (telephone company) exchange office. One-storey red brick Colonial Revival: a steep gable-roofed pavilion on the north half of the road face with a cream lunette over a big gridded (glass-block) window, and a lower hip-roofed south half with a shuttered window, the red 'frontier' sign, a round medallion and a dark side door at the Post Office end. Cream cornice/trim, dark slate roof. Road face -u; left (0) = -v = NNE. OSM's notch at the road/+v corner is not there in the photos (the hip wing is coplanar with the gable), so the block is modelled as a full rectangle.

Detached garage in the back lot behind 53 Prospect St (house 3914 on the overhead). Not legible in any Street View capture: the +u photo shows only a pale blur at the end of the driveway behind the fence, and the yellow lean-to in the -u photo belongs to 60 Genesee. Overhead: dark shingle gable, ridge along u (long axis), gable ends toward the road (+u) and the back lot (-u). Modelled plain: pale warm-grey siding with white trim to match the cream house, dark grey roof, two sectional doors on the +u gable end where the driveway arrives, a man door on the +v (driveway) side.

58-60 West Main St: one OSM footprint holding two attached buildings. Left (+v, NW) half is #60, a long yellow clapboard two-storey house with a squared false front over its street gable and a full-width two-storey porch (open ground floor on thin posts, white balcony rail, yellow-and-white striped awning under the porch roof). Right (-v, SE) half is #58 Puppy's Bar & Grill, a teal front-gabled two-storey with a brick ground floor, a shingled pent canopy and the gold-on-green PUPPY'S sign; a low white shed behind it. Road face is +u (SW, West Main St).

46 W Main St: light blue-grey clapboard 2-storey gable-front duplex, deep plan (23 m) running straight back from the road. Road face +u (SW); left (0) = +v = NW (toward the empty 52 lot / Puppy's). Front gable ~6.4 m wide on the NW side of the OBB: two shuttered (near-black) windows upstairs, a full-width near-flat white porch roof on slim posts with a metal railing, and under it two front doors (dark left, pale right) flanking a window. Behind the front bay the house steps out ~2 m on the SE side (2 storeys, own gable); a low white-roofed garage sits at the rear SE corner with its door facing the road down the driveway. Long NW wall: a row of small upper windows, blank-ish ground floor. Tall column arborvitae at the front NW corner, Dark grey shingle roof.
Avon Farmers Market: one open timber gable shelter with exposed king-post trusses, cafe seating and a low entrance fence. Matched to the user-provided photo.

25 East Main St, corner of Temple St. White clapboard Italianate: a tall 2-storey block on the East Main (+u) end under a low gable with ridge along v, bracketed frieze, an arched attic window in each gable end, and a full-width square-post porch on East Main. Behind it (SSW, -u) a slightly lower 2-storey gabled wing (ridge along u, brick chimney at its junction with the main block) that ends in a one-storey hip-roofed tail. The footprint notch at the -u/+v (Temple St) corner holds a side porch with the side door. Temple St (+v) face carries two faces[].bays: a bracketed one-storey bay window and a glazed one-storey bay at the East Main corner. Road face +v: left (0) = SSW (-u).

Large detached garage behind 25 East Main St at the Temple St corner, west of the house. White clapboard, sea-green standing-seam metal hip roof, ridge along u. Driveway comes down from East Main to the +u (NNE) end, which has one wide dark-green glazed door; -u (SSW, pool side) has a big multi-pane window at the left; -v (WNW, parking-lot side) has two small windows; +v (toward the house) is hidden behind the hedge and left plain.

23 Temple St: 2-storey slate-blue-grey clapboard Victorian with white trim and dark shutters. A steep street-facing cross gable (small arched attic window, pair of shuttered windows) over the NNE half of the front, a hipped main roof, a rear cross gable facing NNE, a red brick chimney on the NNE side near the front, a lower one-storey rear wing. Nearly full-width open front porch with white posts and railing; steps at the NNE end up to the dark front door. Road face -v (Temple St): left (0) = SSW (+u, toward 29 Temple).

Detached garage behind 37 Temple St (the stucco house 248288899 is 2 m off face -v). Gable end to Temple St (+u), ridge along u. Tan vinyl siding, slate-blue trim and fascia, grey shingle roof with wide eaves. +u: one white sectional door left of centre, and the right ~2.8 m (the -v side) is an open carport under the same roof, caricatured as a dark open bay. Other faces plain (no openings visible).

Temple St, north end of the west side (no number in OSM; just SSW of 35 Temple). Tan pebble-dash stucco upright-and-wing: a tall narrow two-storey upright with its gable to the street at the SSW (-v) end — 2 navy-trimmed windows over 2, a small attic vent in the peak — and a low hip-roofed one-storey wing to the NNE (+v) with a flat-roofed open porch (slate-blue posts, white railing) sheltering the white front door and one window. Brick chimney on the wing. Brown shingle roofs. Detached garage behind (248288898) is a separate building. Road face -u; left (0) = -v = SSW.

35 Temple St: white clapboard upright-and-wing farmhouse with black shutters. Road face -v (ESE, Temple St); left (0) = +u = SSW. Upright (street gable, ridge along v) at the NNE (-u) end: 2 shuttered windows over 2 shuttered windows, attic vent in the gable. Lower side-gabled wing to the SSW with a full-width open (screened) porch, front door at the porch's right end against the upright, '35' over it, flag. Tall brick chimney on the wing's SSW gable end. Grey shingle roofs. Low rear extension behind.

33 Temple St: narrow tan 2.5-storey gable-front house (ridge perpendicular to the street), the street gable clad in dark brown shingles with one attic window, dark brown roof, a full-width one-storey open porch with a brown hip roof, cream square posts and railing, steps up to a white door at left-centre. Stone foundation. Rear cross gable and a small hooded side door on the -u (NNE, toward 29 Temple) side. Road face -v; left (0) = +u = SSW (toward 35 Temple).

29 Temple St: pale grey vinyl upright-and-wing farmhouse with brick-red shutters and dark slate window trim. Tall gable-front upright (ridge perpendicular to the street) on the +v (NNE, toward 23 Temple) end of the frontage with 2+2 shuttered windows and a gable vent; lower two-storey wing on the -v side with a dark-posted open porch, one window and the dark red front door tucked against the upright. Long two-storey rear ell on the -v half (rear gable), tall brick chimney and a one-storey bay vestibule on its +v wall. Charcoal roof. Road face -u; left (0) = -v = SSW (toward 33 Temple).

Avon Inn, 55 East Main St. The front is the +u face (NNE, East Main St): five-bay Greek Revival block with a two-storey portico of four giant columns and an AVON INN entablature, the colonnade returning along the Temple St (-v) side of the main block. White clapboard rear wings: a flat-roofed west wing with a bracketed pent roof and stairs on Temple St, a big hip-roofed rear block, and a hip-roofed rear-west wing with a two-storey porch in the notch between them.

36 Temple St: 2-storey tan pebble-dash stucco house, white trim, brown asphalt-shingle roofs, cut-stone foundation. Road face +u (WNW, Temple St); left (0) = +v = NNE. Gable-front upright (steep, ridge along u) on the NNE half of the front: one big ground-floor window, one 2/2 sash above, small attic window in the gable. SSW half is a 2-storey wing under a lower hipped roof; a white-posted hip-roofed porch with railing and frontal steps fills the notch in front of the wing, front door against the upright, flag on a post. Small windows beside the porch at the SSW end. Lower rear ell behind the wing. The yellow house to the SSW is 40 Temple.

40 Temple St: tall 2-storey pale-yellow clapboard gable-front house (ridge along u, steep) under a grey standing-seam metal roof with salmon/rust rakes, corner boards and shutters, a round louvred vent in the street gable, on a dark rubble-stone foundation. Road face +u (WNW, Temple St); left (0) = +v = NNE (toward 36 Temple). Front: a shuttered two-storey window bay at the NNE end, then a one-storey porch on square salmon posts (white caps) over a lattice skirt covering the rest, front door behind it and a run of wooden steps down to the walk; a big red maple in front. Lower rear ell behind. The tan stucco house in the photos is 36 Temple; the blue-grey house is 44.

18 North Avenue: sage-green Dutch Colonial with cream trim. Side gambrel (ridge along u, parallel to the street) with two gabled dormers in the steep front slope, a centred front-facing cross gambrel (barn-shaped gable) with a triple window and attic window, and a full-width raised porch on Tuscan columns with white railing and central steps to a dark oval-glass door. Stone foundation. One-storey rear wing at the east. Body eave at the first floor (3.5 m); the upper floor lives inside the gambrel, its windows in the dormers and in the gambrel ends. Road face +v (west); left (0) = -u = north.

24 North Ave: 2.5-storey gable-front house, tan clapboard with a barn-red shingled front gable and butter-yellow trim; full-width open front porch with four square yellow posts and a red-and-yellow railing, steps to the left-of-centre door; paired attic window in the gable; brick chimney right of the ridge; red wall dormer on the +v (NNE) side toward the rear; rubble-stone foundation. Road face +u; left (0) = +v = NNE.

32 North Ave: compact pale-yellow clapboard 1.75-storey gable-FRONT house (ridge along u, perpendicular to the street), low eaves tucking the second-floor windows under them, wide low-arched attic window in the gable, tall red-brick chimney on the SSW slope near the front and a smaller one at the ridge farther back. Front: white door under a small arched white hood with red-painted steps at LEFT (toward 38 North), a green-trimmed three-window bay under its own little roof right of centre, one narrow window at the far right. Rear hipped, small dormer on the SSW slope, side door with stoop on the NNE side. Road face +u; left (0) = +v = NNE.

Detached two-bay garage at the end of the driveway between 38 North Ave (the ranch 248342249, whose own small attached hip garage is 1.9 m off face +u) and the cream two-storey house 248342246. Gable end to North Avenue (+u), ridge along u. Pale yellow vinyl siding, white trim, grey shingles. +u: two white sectional doors with lights and a small four-pane loft window in the gable. Other faces plain (never seen).

38 North Ave: small one-storey greige vinyl ranch under a low medium-grey hip roof. Front (road face -u): the left ~60% is a shallow open porch (slim posts, near-flat roof) sheltering a wide triple window and the white front door with a black barn star beside it; a twin window to the right of the porch. Lower hip-roofed rear wing offset to the +v (SSW) side, toward the detached garage. Road face -u; left (0) = -v = NNE (toward 42 North). The cream 2.5-storey house in the +v photos is the neighbour 32 North Ave, not this building.

42 North Ave: tall 2.5-storey pale-yellow clapboard Colonial, white trim, slate-teal shutters, dark grey side-gabled roof (ridge along u, parallel to the street) with two gabled dormers on the street slope above the outer bays, brick chimney on the ridge toward the SSW end. Street face (+v): three bays - wide shuttered triple window left, centre door under a small flat portico on two white columns with brick steps, shuttered window right. A one-storey hip-roofed sunroom with tan shades between white pilasters hugs the SSW (+u) end wall, nearly flush with the front. Road face +v; left (0) = -u = NNE (toward 48 North). The grey ranch in the +u photos is 38 North, the pale-blue house in the -u photos is 48 North.

48 North Avenue: light steel-blue vinyl-sided 2.5-storey house, side-gabled (ridge parallel to the street), a semicircular fanlight set in the front roof slope, a brick chimney at the NNE end of the ridge, full-width open front porch with a hip roof, three white posts and a solid siding half-wall (door at the left, wide window at the right, a big blue barn star between). The SSW gable end carries a large dark 3x3 solar-glass panel in the upper storey. A one-storey wing runs back toward the garage. Road face +u; left (0) = +v = NNE (toward 54 North Ave).

54 North Avenue: olive-green clapboard American Foursquare with cream trim; broad hip roof with a wide eave, a hipped dormer with paired windows centred on the front slope, brick chimney near the ridge; full-width open front porch with a hip roof, three square cream posts and a solid siding half-wall, steps at the NNE (driveway) end, dark front door left of centre and a wide triple window right of the middle post; low clipped hedge across the porch front. Small hip-hooded box bay on the SSW side toward the rear; side door on the NNE (driveway) side toward the rear. Road face +u; left (0) = +v = NNE (toward 60 North Ave).

60 North Ave: 2-storey pale peach-beige vinyl colonial, side-gable dark-grey roof with the chimney at the NNE (+u) end of the ridge, three shuttered (near-black) windows upstairs, full-width open porch with white posts and railing on a shallow hip roof, front door at the left (+u) end of the porch, steps there too. A one-storey sun-porch wing on the SSW (-u) side continues the porch roof line. Road face -v; left (0) = +u = NNE (toward 68 North). The blue house in the -v photos is 68 North (+u side), the olive-green Foursquare is 54 North (-u side).

68 North Ave: 2-storey slate-blue vinyl/shingle gable-ell house, white trim, dark-grey steep roofs. Front block A (street end, +u) carries a full-width open porch on a high floor (white posts, railing, white lattice skirt, steps at the NNE/left end, door left of centre, red rocking chairs); its ridge runs parallel to the street (along v) so the gable ends with an attic window face NNE and SSW. Rear block B is offset 3.9 m toward 60 North (-v) and its street-facing gable end peeks out beside the front block from the road. Road face +u; left (0) = +v = NNE (toward 72 North). The pale colonial in the -v photos is 60 North (248342255), the grey colonial in the +v photos is the next house NNE.

37 North Avenue: one-storey beige vinyl ranch set 40 m back from the road behind a big tree. T-plan: hip-roofed bar along the NNE (-v) side, gabled stem toward the SSW (+v) with two arched-head windows in its gable end, small gabled entry at the inside corner. +u = ESE (road), +v = SSW.

55 North Ave: tan stucco 2-storey Colonial Revival box under a silver standing-seam side-gable roof (ridge along u, parallel to the street). Three-bay front: wide triple windows flanking a centred door with sidelights and a gabled white two-column portico; three 1/1 sash upstairs. Long orange wooden wheelchair ramp from the sidewalk to the door. One-storey glazed sun porch with a silver hip roof on the +u (SSW, left-as-seen-from-street) side near the front. Road face -v; left (0) = +u = SSW.

61 North Ave: 1.5-storey grey-beige clapboard Craftsman bungalow, side-gable roof (ridge along v, parallel to the street) sweeping down over a full-width ENCLOSED front porch; a wide 3-window shed dormer centred in the front slope; brick chimney at the ridge right of centre. Front: triple window | centred pale door up 4 steps | triple window, between two sided corner piers. Grey block foundation. Small bay windows at the porch ends on both sides; side door with stoop on +v. Road face -u; left (0) = -v = SSW.

65 East Main St: NOT brick - a pale yellow-green clapboard two-storey house with a low hip roof and cream trim, converted to a shop. A one-storey enclosed front porch with a hip roof runs the full width and wraps into a one-storey east (+v) wing; two big dark-framed display windows and a centre-left cream door with steps sit under it. A two-storey gabled rear wing behind. Road face is +u (NNE, East Main St); the Avon Inn is the -v neighbour.

Small grey-roofed outbuilding/garage in the parking lot behind the Park Theater block (1090362840). Not visible in any Street View capture; modelled plain from the overhead. Road face +v faces the back of the theater; doors put on the parking-lot sides (-v, +u).

75 West Main St, the red building at the West Main / South Ave corner: a 2-storey barn-red brick house-form with a steep red standing-seam gable roof (ridge along u) whose front gable (+u, West Main side) is tan shingle with a paired window. Across the +u front, a two-storey porch: the ground floor is enclosed in cream clapboard with a big display window and a door, the upper floor an open balcony with cream posts and a white railing under the roof. A low 1-storey cream-sided rear wing with a red gable roof runs back (-u) toward the South Ave parking lot. Small cream gabled side entry on -v. Brief calls +v (South Ave) the road face, but the front is +u.

67 West Main St (sits on the South Ave frontage): pale cream clapboard 2-storey house with mauve-pink shutters. A taller square block at the SW (-u) end wears a very low cross-gabled roof with deep boxed eaves (Italianate pediments on -u and +v) and a small hip-roofed open porch with thin iron posts across its street face; a lower 2-storey gabled wing (ridge along the street) runs NE with two shuttered windows up, one shuttered window and a shuttered bay window down, and a hedge under them. Road face +v; left (0) = -u = SW.

15 South Ave: small white clapboard gable-front-and-wing house. Road face -v (ESE, South Avenue); left (0) = +u = SSW. Upright with the street gable at the SSW (+u) end: 2 shuttered windows over 2 shuttered windows. Lower side-gabled wing to the NNE with a wide triple window over the front door under a little gabled hood ('15'). One-storey sunroom further NNE, set back. The OSM polygon also swallows the detached garage behind the sunroom (the u<-3 lobe): white gable-front garage with a big sectional door facing the street, driveway along the NNE side. Brick chimney on the wing ridge next to the upright.
Edward Jones office, 87 Genesee St. Road face -v. Tan clapboard over red brick on the street front only; buff brick side and rear walls. Flat roof, chimney on the -u side near the front.

77 Genesee St: NYS Assemblywoman Andrea Bailey's district office. Narrow 2-storey gable-front (ridge running back from the street) in grey-beige brick; ground floor storefront with vertical blinds between rock-faced tan stone piers, glass door + white apartment door at the right, white fascia with the navy office sign; three tall white windows upstairs; white raking fascia on the gable. Party wall with the Park Theater block (1090362840) on -v; alley on +v. Road face +u; left (0) = +v = SSW.

Avon Park Theater (71 Genesee, 1938) + two absorbed neighbours to its north: the narrow white flat-roof 2-storey (Integrity Tours / 'Wedding Flowers by Avon Floral World') and the white clapboard gable of Avon Floral World (63 Genesee). Road face +u; left (fraction 0) = +v = SSW.
